plan.spine_question: Which part of casting out a demon actually does the work, the prayer or the paperwork behind it?
plan.payoff_line: The ritual never really changed. What changed is who signs for it now.

deflations.assumed: Becoming an exorcist meant receiving a rare spiritual gift, power over demons
deflations.actual: For centuries nearly every priesthood candidate received the same exorcist title as a routine step, and most never used it before it was abolished
deflations.who_decided: The Church's traditional four minor orders, porter, lector, exorcist, acolyte, assigned the title to seminary candidates automatically until Pope Paul VI abolished the minor orders in 1972

deflations.assumed: The exorcism rite was a fixed, unchanging secret spell handed down whole
deflations.actual: The rite is a printed manual, revised more than once, and the original 1614 text itself told the priest to check for sickness before assuming possession
deflations.who_decided: The Rituale Romanum's own printed instructions, issued under Pope Paul V in 1614

deflations.assumed: One priest ended a possession alone, in a single dramatic night
deflations.actual: The Archbishop of Saint Louis only granted permission on condition a diary be kept, and multiple priests logged more than twenty sessions over about two months
deflations.who_decided: The Archbishop of Saint Louis, who required the written diary as the condition for permission, recorded by Father Raymond Bishop

deflations.assumed: Priests forced the ritual on a helpless girl against her will
deflations.actual: Anneliese Michel was an adult who herself refused to see a doctor as the sessions went on, and the court later found medical help, not the ritual, was the missing factor
deflations.who_decided: Anneliese Michel's own refusal of medical treatment, and the Aschaffenburg court's finding that a doctor could likely have saved her

deflations.assumed: A modern court like this one finally ended the whole practice for good
deflations.actual: Rome kept its own exorcist working for decades afterward, and even a canon lawyer inside the Church doubted his own numbers
deflations.who_decided: Gabriele Amorth, appointed exorcist for the diocese of Rome in 1986 and active until his death in 2016; canon lawyer Edward Peters publicly questioned Amorth's count

specifics.fact: On 17 June 1614 Pope Paul V authorized the first official edition of the Rituale Romanum by the constitution Apostolicae Sedis
In 1952 two small language revisions were made to the Rituale Romanum, the first change since 1614
On 26 January 1999 the Vatican issued an 84-page revised edition of the exorcism rite, De Exorcismis et Supplicationibus Quibusdam
specifics.source: Wikipedia: Of Exorcisms and Certain Supplications

specifics.fact: The minor orders, including exorcist, belonged to the Church's ordination structure for at least seventeen hundred years before being set aside
specifics.source: New Liturgical Movement: 50 Years Ago Today

specifics.fact: On 15 August 1972 Pope Paul VI signed Ministeria Quaedam, abolishing the minor orders of porter, lector, exorcist, and acolyte, effective 1 January 1973
The Archbishop of Saint Louis granted permission for a secret exorcism only on condition that a detailed diary be kept
specifics.source: Exorcism of Roland Doe case document, citing Father Raymond Bishop's diary (Scribd)

specifics.fact: Father William Bowdern and fellow priests performed more than twenty documented exorcism sessions over about two months in 1949
specifics.source: Skeptical Inquirer: Demoniac, Who Is Roland Doe

specifics.fact: Bishop Josef Stangl approved the exorcism of Anneliese Michel after doctors had failed to stop her convulsions
specifics.source: Medium: Mental Illness or Demonic Possession, Anneliese Michel

specifics.fact: Anneliese Michel herself asked not to see a doctor as the exorcism sessions continued through her final months
specifics.source: Medium: She Endured 67 Exorcisms, Then Starved to Death

specifics.fact: Fathers Arnold Renz and Ernst Alt performed sixty seven exorcism sessions on Anneliese Michel over about ten months
Anneliese Michel weighed about sixty eight pounds when she died on 1 July 1976
Investigators concluded Anneliese Michel could likely have survived if a doctor had been called even a week before her death
specifics.source: Medium: She Endured 67 Exorcisms, Then Starved to Death

specifics.fact: Gabriele Amorth, exorcist for the diocese of Rome from 1986, claimed to have performed more than sixty thousand exorcism sessions
specifics.source: The Conversation: Gabriele Amorth conducted over 60,000 exorcisms

specifics.fact: Canon lawyer Edward Peters called Amorth's claim of thirty thousand personal exorcisms over nine years astounding, since Amorth himself said fewer than one hundred involved actual possession

beats.location: a mudbrick healer's house beside the Tigris river
beats.narration: Most people think exorcism began with the Catholic Church itself.

beats.location: a mudbrick healer's house beside the Tigris river
beats.narration: [flatly] It is much older than that.

beats.location: a mudbrick healer's house beside the Tigris river
beats.narration: One ancient healer treated fever and demons in the same single visit.

beats.location: a mudbrick healer's house beside the Tigris river
beats.narration: So which part actually worked?

beats.location: a mudbrick healer's house beside the Tigris river
beats.narration: [curious] An ashipu was part doctor, part priest, treating fever as possession.

beats.location: a mudbrick healer's house beside the Tigris river
beats.narration: Amulets and chants counted as medicine.

beats.location: a mudbrick healer's house beside the Tigris river
beats.narration: The Greek word daimon, root of demon, could mean good or evil.

beats.location: a mudbrick healer's house beside the Tigris river
beats.narration: [flatly] Rome later borrowed that word.

beats.location: a mudbrick healer's house beside the Tigris river
beats.narration: Centuries later the followers of Jesus took up the same practice.

beats.location: a signing chamber inside Saint Peter's Basilica
beats.narration: By sixteen fourteen the Church wanted one approved script for priests.

beats.location: a signing chamber inside Saint Peter's Basilica
beats.narration: [flatly] Pope Paul the Fifth signed it.

beats.location: a signing chamber inside Saint Peter's Basilica
beats.narration: The order was given at Rome, at Saint Peters, under his seal.

beats.location: a signing chamber inside Saint Peter's Basilica
beats.narration: The instructions were strict and specific.

beats.location: a signing chamber inside Saint Peter's Basilica
beats.narration: Many still picture the rite as a fixed secret spell, unchanged forever.

beats.location: a signing chamber inside Saint Peter's Basilica
beats.narration: [deadpan] It told him to check for sickness first.

beats.location: a signing chamber inside Saint Peter's Basilica
beats.narration: More than three centuries passed before Rome changed a single word.

beats.location: a signing chamber inside Saint Peter's Basilica
beats.narration: Then two words were quietly updated.

beats.location: a signing chamber inside Saint Peter's Basilica
beats.narration: [flatly] By nineteen ninety nine the exorcism section became an eighty four page document.
For at least seventeen hundred years, exorcist required no special calling.
It was one stop toward priesthood.
Picture a seminarian kneeling to receive a rare gift, power over demons.
[flatly] Nearly every candidate got the same title.
The words stayed the same for centuries, a formula and a gesture.
[deadpan] Most never touched a real case.
In nineteen seventy two Pope Paul the Sixth erased the minor orders.
Exorcist stopped being a step.
[flatly] From then on, only a priest with written permission could try one.

beats.location: a Jesuit hospital ward in Saint Louis
beats.narration: In nineteen forty nine a Missouri family asked the Jesuits for help.

beats.location: a Jesuit hospital ward in Saint Louis
beats.narration: Doctors and ministers had failed.

beats.location: a Jesuit hospital ward in Saint Louis
beats.narration: [deadpan] Picture one priest locked in a room, ending it in a single night.

beats.location: a Jesuit hospital ward in Saint Louis
beats.narration: [deadpan] The archbishop demanded a written diary first.

beats.location: a Jesuit hospital ward in Saint Louis
beats.narration: Father Raymond Bishop wrote down every session exactly as it happened.

beats.location: a Jesuit hospital ward in Saint Louis
beats.narration: [surprised] The rite ran more than twenty times.

beats.location: a Jesuit hospital ward in Saint Louis
beats.narration: Three priests rotated through the vigil, each one logging that night.

beats.location: a Jesuit hospital ward in Saint Louis
beats.narration: No single hero performed the rite.

beats.location: a Jesuit hospital ward in Saint Louis
beats.narration: [sad] Decades later another family trusted the same church for a different ordeal.
A German student named Anneliese Michel had already seen doctors for years.
Seizures had started at sixteen.
[sighs] Doctors diagnosed epilepsy, but the fits kept returning despite treatment.
Bishop Josef Stangl finally approved an exorcism.
Picture two priests overpowering a helpless girl, forcing ritual against her will.
[deadpan] She refused to see a doctor herself.
Over ten months the two priests performed sixty seven exorcism sessions.
She stopped eating in her final months.
[sad] By July she weighed about sixty eight pounds, like a large dog.
She died on the first of July.
Two years later a court in Aschaffenburg heard the parents and priests.
[flatly] All four faced negligent homicide charges.
The court found medical help could likely have saved her.
Not the ritual, but the delay.
Many assume a modern court like this one ended the whole practice.
[deadpan] Rome's own exorcist kept working for decades.
Gabriele Amorth, the diocese of Rome's exorcist, claimed sixty thousand sessions himself.
[sarcastic] A church lawyer called the count astounding.
The ritual never really changed. What changed is who signs for it now.
